It's a different bank run by entirely different people, right?
Well, not exactly.
The same people who ran the economy into the ground betting on dangerous securities might have done the same thing again.
That's right, Joseph Gentile, one of the executives at SVB, used to also be an executive for Lehman Brothers.
As their chief financial officer, he oversaw the most disastrous banking collapse in history.
And now he's done it again in nearly exactly the same way.

And then the final nail in the coffin came when SVB's CEO announced that they would be selling ownership of the company to raise $2.25 billion after taking losses of over $1.5 billion in failed bond positions.
Once word of this got out the day after the announcement, it caused the company stock to dump over 60% when the insolvacy issues went public.
Then on March 10th, the CEO announced they had failed to raise enough capital for recovery.
In a desperate move, they were looking for another company to take over SVB.
However, by this time, it was too late, and the government stepped in and seized the bank.
Even worse for SVB, almost 100% of their business accounts are not covered by the FDIC's insurance.
FDIC insurance only covers up to $250,000, dollars, a number that is far too small for the 97.3% of SVB accounts, which are worth a lot more than this.
Meaning the majority of companies being held by SVB are now unable to access their money, since it's not covered by insurance.
So these subordinate companies may go under simply because they cannot access their own money.
And now who's to blame for this?
Well, the blame rests squarely on SVB's shoulders.

The bank made incredibly poor decisions to bet entirely on the Federal Reserve's interest rate not to be raised, rather than diversifying their investments like the majority of other banking institutions.

Because of this, their assets cannot be properly liquidated in time for clients to get their funding withdrawn, meaning many of the held companies are now going to have to wait a very long time to get their money back.
And we're talking about companies like Etsy, Circle, Roblox and BlockFi, which had hundreds of millions in SUV, which they might never see again.
Regulators have had to step in to shut down the bank and to oversee what's left of the bank's assets.
Employees at the bank have been offered 1.5 times their salary for the next 45 days if they stay on to manage the funeral proceedings.
And it's unclear how much they'll be up to save considering how desperate the situation truly is.

title: One of These Countries Will Collapse in 1 Year
note: A ranked tour of countries near economic collapse, escalating to Pakistan as the worst, with a mid-film sponsor read; each country section opens with a why/how question and answers it.
sections: South Africa: inequality and failing services
lines: One of these countries' economies is about to crash within the next couple of years.
And a perfect example of this is South Africa.
Blackouts and riots, looting and poverty.
South Africa is undoubtedly in a very rough place.
But the most visible problem within the country is inequality, which is now at its highest levels in decades.
Because the richest 10% of the population now own over 85% of household wealth, with 3,500 of the wealthiest South Africans owning more than the poorest 32 million put together.
To put into context, this is over half of the country's population.
Unemployment is also a massive problem here, with over 60% of the country's young people not even having a job.
The divisions between the rich and poor are plain to see.
Just a few meters separates completely different worlds.
And with no hope of a brighter future, millions of young South Africans have turned to violent crime to make their living.

An endemic culture of gang warfare and violence is festered across the nation, culminating in an infamous spree of violent crime and rioting, making South Africa infamous for being one of the world's most dangerous countries.
And now the strain on essential national services is also reaching critical levels.
In fact, flights were recently grounded at Cape Town International Airport after a shortage of jet fuel.
And so it's no surprise that the education system is now one of the worst in the world because of the government's negligent underfunding.

Recent testing showed that over a quarter of children in school for over six years still couldn't read, leaving the next generation of South Africans sorely underprepared to tackle the problems of the future.

And in the face of all of these mounting problems, the government has been grossly incompetent, becoming infamous for a history of dodging problems by creating entirely new ones, like when they banned alcohol during lockdowns, putting thousands of livelihoods in danger for no real reason.
And because of these systemic issues, economists are now predicting yet another recession in South Africa this year, on top of their already disastrous economy.
And now why is this happening in South Africa?
Well, the main reason for this is the all-encompassing web of corruption that has brought South Africa's economy to its knees.
In the country, it affects all levels of society.

At the top, you can see corruption at the state monopoly power company Exxon, which has led to years of gross incompetence, where vital repairs to infrastructure were postponed or cancelled, all in order to siphon off more funds, leaving South Africa's entire energy grid physically incapable of supplying a hungry, growing country.
And that's why in the last couple of years, South Africa has faced bouts of 12-hour-long blackouts.
And they've just been getting worse.
there were four and a half times as many in 2022 compared to 2021.
And in this year of 2023, it's expected to get even worse.
I mean, South Africa has been blinded by corruption, and there's really no rush at the top to fix things.

Instead, those at the top are focused on petty power struggles and schemes, with one of the previous chief executives of Exxon being poisoned with cyanide, presumably by his rivals in the company, as he was fired just months later after denying corruption charges.
However, there is some light to hope in South Africa.
People are fighting back, like Babita Diokaran.
Over the course of 30 years, she has built a career as a public servant, fighting South Africa's corruption.
She was pivotal in uncovering a corrupt scheme that stopped 500 million South African rand from hospitals, equivalent to nearly 30 million dollars.
And Babita's reward for this work came a year later, when she was gunned down in broad daylight on the 23rd of August 2021, after dropping off her daughter at school.
And despite her status as a whistleblower, the government had offered her no protection.
And after investigations concluded, the person who hired the hit has escaped justice.
However, 6,500 miles away in North Africa, things aren't looking too good either.
Anyone can find anything on the internet, including your full legal name, your personal email, your home address, phone number, and even your relatives.
This information is accessible because of data brokers, who profit by selling your information to robocallers, telemarketers, spammers, and anyone else that wants to learn more about you.
Rising costs and stagnating wages have created a death spiral of poverty.
And no country better illustrates this than the savage cycle that Tunisia is facing, where their economic outlook is particularly dire.

You see, the country's public debt was already at 70% of the nation's GDP, a staggering amount that's now risen to nearly 90% since then, a number that has massively increased in just a matter of years.

So it's no surprise that poverty rates have also jumped above 15%, just 10 years after the Tunisian revolution, a revolution that was partially incited by worsening economic conditions in the company just a decade ago.
But now Tunisians are back to seeing severe shortages of fuel, flour, bread, sugar and other essential supplies.
And that's on top of the regular droughts they face in the country.
And so that begs the question, what kind of government can Tunisian people turn to in its time of need?

When unfortunately, the democratic ideals of the revolution that happened in 2011 have already quickly been cast aside, as last year Tunisia's 10-year experiment with democracy was cut short by a dictatorial coup.
Kaysiyad is the new man in power, after seizing it in a bloodless coup just a few years after he won the presidency.
And he hasn't been shy about cracking down on political opponents with mass arrests.
He's even arresting people critical of the regime on social media.
And the political instability hasn't made things any better.
Mass protests and strikes have ground the economy to a halt.
And Seed's solution for this country's woes is a hard and long austerity program, designed to cut the basic support that Danissia still gives to its people.
Subsidies on clean drinking water are being slashed, for example, leading to a $23 increase in water prices nationwide.
And overall spending on subsidies will be slashed by 26.4%, or taxes will rise by 12.5%.
These plan reforms convinced the IMF to go forward with an emergency loan of $1.8 billion.
But the recent instability has led to delays, as well as cutting all of Tunisia's tourism money.

And that's why no many creditors even want to invest in a country on the brink of economic collapse, causing Tunisia's credit rating to recently be downgraded again, signaling a high risk that any loans to Tunisia will be defaulted on.
And whether Tunisia's new autocratic government will survive the coming crisis is a complete mystery.
The only thing that is clear is that Tunisia is dangerously close to bankruptcy.
But there's still countries that are further along the road to disaster than Tunisia.
In fact, Lebanon has gone from crisis to crisis for years, causing 80% of the population to land in poverty.
Things have gotten so bad that clean water shortages have become the norm, giving rise to one of the worst cholera outbreaks in decades.
In fact, this current crisis is the worst they've ever seen, which is why Lebanon's currency has completely collapsed.
In fact, the government recently devalued it by 90% and it still hasn't caught up to the real scale of inflation.
So in response, the banks have been blocking people from withdrawing their savings without taking a massive portion of it.
And the only way that anyone's gotten their money back is by taking it back from the bank at gunpoint.
Although in this case, it's really the reverse of theft.
So then why has inflation gotten so bad in Lebanon?
It's almost like the economy was pushed towards collapse.
Well, there's several reasons.
The first reason that elites in Lebanon point to is external factors like the war in neighboring countries like Syria.
In addition to the COVID pandemic, as the causes behind their economic chaos.

But like all good lies, this is only half of the picture, as the World Bank has called Lebanon's inflation crisis a deliberate depression by the financial elite, likening what they did to a Ponzi scheme.
Because you see, before the war in Syria and the pandemic, the Lebanese government spent years making hollow promises to investors in exchange for massive loans.
They created an illusion of a healthy currency by constantly propping up its value with further loans.
In a classic Ponzi scheme cycle, they would choose new loans to pay off old ones.
And like all Ponzi schemes, it eventually came to an explosive end, when Lebanon could no longer justify more loans.
The war and the pandemic made investors so much more cautious in the country, which eventually sent the economy into a death spiral.
Just before the beginning of the crisis in 2019, Lebanon's debt had reached 171% of its GDP.
And then it all collapsed, the scam fell apart, and Lebanon's people were left to pick up the pieces.
And the tragedy of the 2020 Beirut explosion came as a deadly reminder of the cost of corruption.

All in order to save money, port officials had overlooked the dangerous dumping of volatile explosives in an old warehouse, leading to 218 people losing their lives in the explosion, and over 7,000 more were injured.
But if you thought Lebanon had reached rock bottom, you're wrong, because without a concrete plan in place, the crisis is only going to keep on going.

Now, Lebanon is trying to get a multi-billion dollar bailout package from the IMF, but it hasn't gone through yet, and so investors are understandably nervous about investing in a government that has been scamming its people for decades.
And so without massive reforms and this bailout, Lebanon's future is looking very grim.
Whilst Argentina may not be as far gone as Lebanon or Tunisia right now, their future collapse could be far more catastrophic.
You see, their debt problem has been festering away for years, and now it's starting to have very serious effects on their economy.
Which is why inflation has reached a high of 95% annually last year, which meant that Argentinian people lost half of their savings in the space of one year.
Now obviously the people have been suffering.
Homelessness has has risen massively as more people fall through the widening cracks in the system.
It's also why nearly 40% of Argentinians now live below the poverty line, and the worst drought in 60 years has cost the country $20 billion.
So to put it simply, things suck right now.

But the real problem lies in Argentina's massive debt and how they're going to repay it, because they borrowed $57 billion in 2018 through an IMF bailout, and they've been struggling to pay it back ever since.
And this comes after restructuring last year, which helped delay the problem.
And whether they can keep up with repayments though is a whole other matter.
As economic growth is also predicted to slow in Argentina, going from nearly 5% to just 2%, with some outlets predicting a further drop to just 1% growth.
Unemployment, which was falling in recent years, has just started picking up again as well.
And these predicted gains are nearly enough to keep the Argentinian economy afloat in the face of a total of $174 billion in debt.
I mean, there's already discussions now on whether they've already technically defaulted on it.
The government has been buying back debt at a crazy rate, sparking fears that it's all getting too much for the government.
And it shows in the hyperinflation, which has gotten to the point that it's cheaper to use a 10 peso bill rather than buying actual wallpaper.
You see, this is where the real problem lies with Argentina's economy.
Both foreign investors and the people have very little confidence in the government's ability to navigate in the country out of the storm.
This means that foreign investors are increasingly unlikely to offer the country much needed aid.
But on a domestic level, it's played havoc on the country's politics.
years of economic degradation have left the country incredibly polarized, turning every political issue into a societal schism.
And with this polarization comes mass protests, that we're likely to see a repeat of the demonstrations that brought the country to the standstill over 2020 and 2021.
For a country that should be able to fall back on a wealth of natural resources, Argentina is incredibly close to bankruptcy.
However, if you take bankruptcy as literally running out of cash, Nigeria has everyone beaten.
Along with a slew of long-term economic problems, Nigeria has created another crisis out of thin air by running out of paper notes.
55% of Nigeria's population doesn't have access to banking, meaning that they've been left without money in the midst of an economic crisis.
Markets that were busy just days ago were virtually abandoned.
Nobody can pay for anything.
People are waiting in line for hours at the bank or ATM just to get enough money to last the day.
So how did this even happen?
Well, it started in October when Nigeria's government made the bold decision to replace all of the highest nomination nodes in their currency.
Worse still, the government gave people just three months before the old notes became worthless.
There was an immediate rush to get the new notes, but the government hadn't made nearly enough of them.
The move came as part of a misguided grander plan to make Nigeria a cashless society.
However, clearly, cash is still needed as shown by the months of chaos.
And to their credit, when the cash ran out, lots turned to a different kind of cashless transaction, bartering.
They were later forced to move the deadline further and further up as the crisis continued.
And as a result of this crisis, private sector growth stopped for the first time in three years.
But why is the government so desperate to fix what isn't broken?
Well, it's part of yet another hollow policy to make it look like Nigeria's government is addressing their endemic corruption problem.
Without cash, certain types of money laundering and lower level corruption tactics would get much harder.
But it doesn't do anything to stop the most harmful institutional corruption that goes on at the highest levels of government.
One example is the ex-Accountant General of Federation Ahamed Idris, who was arrested on corruption charges in May of 2022.
He was accused of masterminding a fraud campaign, which strained the equivalent of $236 million from public funds, and it's pretty unlucky that this bit of corruption was conducted using cash.
In total, an estimated 170 million bribes are paid in Nigeria every year, as corruption affects every level of society, and it's playing havoc on an already shaky economy.
Poverty rates in Nigeria keep on rising, with recent estimates putting the total amount of 133 million Nigerians living in poverty.
Sortages are also common, especially concerning fuel, and in a country which produces massive quantities of oil, this shouldn't be happening.
But politicians like Ahmed Idris have created a system of fraud where they can sell the oil cheaply to Western companies, all whilst taking a cut for themselves.
And this comes at the expense of the people.
And with major reforms, the newly elected government does hope to pull the country back from the edge.
But this all-too-familiar debt problem means the way out will be long and hard, as climbing debt repayments could quickly outpace the economy's ability to handle them.
And judging by the recent dips in the Nigerian bond market, financial analysis doubt that they have what it takes.
But at least there is a way out for Nigeria, whereas Pakistan's future looks far more bleak.
The economy is in the ICU, the politicians are at war, and the people are crying for help.
It's one hell of a mess.
Fuel shortages are the first of many problems, with rising costs putting an end to lots of businesses' ability to just function, which as a result meant that jobs have been lost at an alarming rate.
In October of 2022, it was announced that over 1,600 textile mills had been closed, all because of fuel shortages, which resulted in 5 million people losing their jobs.
And as unemployment skyrockets and wages stagnate, inflation has soared to 40%, the highest it's ever been since the 70s in Pakistan.
And this combination of inflation and unemployment has left millions without basic necessities like food, shelter and basic medical care.

And as if this wasn't enough, huge floods have ravaged the country in recent months, with one third of the country becoming submerged in water, killing or injuring 15,000 people and displacing a further 8 million.
And so as always, the overall crisis is framed by a massive amount of debt which is strangling the economy.
In fact, over the last 25 years, Pakistan's national debt has doubled every 5 years.
This 14% annual growth in debt completely outweighs the average 3% annual GDP growth.
And so it was only a matter of time before Pakistan's economy was just unable to keep up.
And so now the government is dangerously low on cash.
There's just 3 billion dollars left for a country that has a population of over 230 million people.
And so to keep some semblance of order, Pakistan's government has been waiting on a 1.1 billion dollar bayout, which is just one part of a larger rescue plan.
However, the IMF has been holding it back, demanding harsher measures like tax increases and fuel price hikes to stave off the collapse.
And this financial limbo has been poisonous for Pakistan's recovery, as the value of Pakistan's rupee dropped by 9.6 the day that the IMF's measures were put in place.
And that's why the government is on its last legs trying to deal with this fallout, but the crisis has also led to major political upheaval.
Former Prime Minister Imran Khan has been leading protests against the current regime, calling for fundamental rights for Pakistan's people.
Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan is leading a march of his supporters from the eastern city of Lahore to the capital Islamabad, demanding early elections.
And he was the president just a year ago, and that's why this represents an existential threat for the current government.
And so as a result, the government has issued an arrest warrant for former prime minister and has cracked down on protesters with tear gas and hoses.
And it's not hard to see why so many people blame the government for the crisis.
Years of corruption and reckless borrowing have pushed the country over the edge.
Mass poverty, an angry populace, and a government in turmoil are a recipe for disaster, making a complete collapse more likely every single day.
And the implications for this would be massive.
Pakistan's 230 million people are in desperate need and a further collapse would create a humanitarian crisis of unimaginable proportions.

And we shouldn't forget that Pakistan is also a nuclear state, meaning that its fights were that the keys to power are closely watched, as right now Pakistan faces the perfect conditions for a coup, and a new regime could upset the delicate balance of power between Pakistan, India and China.
And so with their crisis deepening every day, it's no surprise that Pakistan is the closest to bankruptcy of all the countries that we've spoken about.

title: How Kim-Jong-Un Stole $1 Billion in 48 Hours
note: A heist narrative (setup, dormant virus, the Feb 2016 attack, luck and mistakes, laundering) followed by a long explainer on Lazarus, its hackers and North Korea's regime and economy, with a mid-film sponsor read.
sections: The intrusion and the SWIFT attack
Jupiter Street blocks and the typo
Who was behind it: Park Jin Hyok and the hacker pipeline
Other Lazarus attacks and crypto theft
North Korea's other crimes and money needs
Regime control and why hackers comply
lines: North Korea needed cash and fast.
You see, they'd been sanctioned like no other country.
With every single export being blocked, no country trading with them, and being shunned by the global economy, their country was now starving.
And the outlook was very bleak.
So running out of options, King Timur needed to find some money fast.
So he decided to attempt the biggest bank heist in history.
But he obviously wasn't going to do it all by himself.
Instead, he turned to his personal army of cybercriminals, the Lazarus Group.
For 10 years, the Lazarus Group have terrorized financial institutions across the world in a series of brutal cyber attacks.
Although they've largely kept their identities a mystery, their origins can be traced back to North Korea's top secret cyber criminal program, also known as the 414 Liaison Office.
Now it's not really known how they first gained access to the Bangladesh Bank's systems, but there are a couple of ways they could have got in.
The first was a suspicious email sent out to Bangladesh Bank employees a year prior.
In January 2015, a seemingly innocuous job application from a man called Rasal Alam popped up in some employees' inboxes.
It included a message about his credentials, and invited them to download a document with a CV attached.
But inside that document, an invader was lurking and once it was in the system, it got straight to work, metastasizing itself inside of the network.
But just as it gained complete control of the bank's systems, it suddenly stopped.
It wasn't time yet.
The virus needed to lay dormant until the perfect opportunity, and that wouldn't come for another year.
In fact, there's evidence that this was one point of intrusion, but there's also the possibility that it was an inside job.

Investigators have long suspected that someone at the bank had to be involved, as only someone with intimate knowledge of the bank's security measures could have known how to pull off what happened next.
And as we'll learn later on, the Lazarus Group had agents in other banks.
However, other than a few dismissals, nobody at the Bangladesh Central Bank has been punished for the intrusion.
So, the hackers lay dormant within the bank's network for nearly a year.
But by January 29th, 2016, the virus was on the move again.
This time it tried to get from the bank's network into the SWIFT system.
Now for those who don't know, SWIFT is a program used by banks to send money securely across the world.
All ATMs rely on SWIFT, as this records all global transactions across banking networks.
It will create digital receipts and add them to the record, whilst also printing out a paper copy of each large transaction.
At first, SWIFT rejected the hacker's attempts to log in.
It kept finding problems with their credentials and permissions, but after at least four failed attempts, they finally made it in and hastily covered their tracks.
And it was only after the attack was over that investigators found evidence of these intrusions.
Then a few days after they got into SWIFT, the Lazarus Group was ready to put their plan into action.
All they needed to do was make the transaction request and hope.
But there was a reason the Lazarus Group had risked being discovered for nearly a year.
They were waiting for the stars to align.
And eventually they found their perfect moment, with the hack beginning at 8pm on Thursday, the 4th of February 2016, just after business closed at the Bangladesh Bank.
Suddenly, 35 fraudulent multi-million dollar transactions flooded out of the bank.
Made to look legit by the hackers infiltration of the SWIFT system, they also made sure that the Bangladesh Bank wouldn't discover the transactions until it was too late.
They did this by wiping the logs and sabotaging the printer to delay the physical failsafe.

However, it was still early in the day in New York, where the money was actually held and the transactions were processed, so this gave plenty of time for the Federal Reserve to send their money out into the world.
The next day was the beginning of the Bangladeshi weekend, meaning nobody would really be around to notice what just happened.
Then the day after that, on the Saturday, only a skeleton crew came in to oversee what's usually a quiet day.
And it was that afternoon when they got the printers working again, that they discovered the true magnitude of what had just happened.
In total, the Lazarus Group had taken $951 million from their account.
But Bangladesh's central bank was about to have their first bit of good luck.
When the Federal Reserve received the transaction requests, most of them were made out to the RCBC bank on Jupiter Street, Manila.
Now this is a completely legitimate bank, so it shouldn't have raised any flags.
However, there is also a sanctioned Iranian shipping vessel that's also called Jupiter.
So the Fed system saw the word Jupiter, flagged the transactions and blocked them.
So only 5 of the 35 transactions got through because of just a complete coincidence in the system.
And so by choosing this one bank over hundreds of others in Manila alone cost the hackers around $850 million.
But the hackers still had $100 million left and the clock was ticking.
By February 9th, officials at the bank in Bangladesh had seen the flyer of messages from the Federal Reserve.
Panicked, they sent stop orders to the rest of the transactions.
But for most of them, it was too late.
One of the five that did get through though, was sent along to a charity called the Shalika Foundation.
They were meant to pass on this $20 million donation further down the line, but it never got there in the first place.
And despite the intricate planning and sophistication that went into the heist, the Lazarus group made a stupid mistake, and it would cost them big time.
As on the transfer request, the hackers had misspelled foundation on the transfer order, writing it instead as foundation.
An eagle-eyed bank employee spotted the error and stole the transaction just in time to freeze the funds.
So the hackers had just lost another $20 million, and it was all just because of a simple typo.
However, they still left $80 million that was uncounted for, and getting further out of reach every minute that was still missing.
But the bank manager didn't let anyone else know, besides the security consultants he brought in to investigate.
In fact, the whole scandal was kept under wraps during the most vital hours of the investigation.
When the security consultants did finally arrive, all they could do was trace the path that the money took.
So this gave the hackers all the time they needed to withdraw their funds and get them out as soon as possible.
And it was only on the 9th of February, five full days after the attack, that Bangladesh sent freeze requests to the Jupiter Street Bank.
But despite the freeze requests received a few hours earlier, the Jupiter Street Bank manager authorised the withdrawal of all the funds from the suspect accounts.
And because of this, she was later convicted for her part in the crime.
Without her approval of the withdrawal, a large portion of this money would have been reclaimed.
However, the Lazarus Group had lost hundreds of millions in potential takings, but they did still have 81 million dollars of stolen money within their reach.
However, if they kept it in the legitimate financial world forever, it would eventually be traced and seized by authorities.
So they needed to come up with a plan to take it out and make it look clean.
And they found that the best way to do this was through gambling.
Casinos, or at least the kind that the Lazarus Group went to, aren't very scrupulous about where you get your money.
The Seler and Midas Casino in Manila were happy to take 50 million of the Lazarus Group's money, all without any questions being asked.

And once they were in the casino's private rooms, the Lazarus Group stacked a card table with accomplices, and by controlling the game, the hackers could get nearly all of their money back as clean casino winnings, ready to be shipped back straight to North Korea.

At the time, the Philippines had very relaxed money laundering laws for casinos, meaning it was impossible for the Bangladeshi authorities to get their money back without a long and drawn-out legal battle.
But by then, it would be gone forever, and lost in the helmet kingdom.

Although some of the money was still recovered after a casino manager brought it to authorities, but most of the stolen money made its way out of the casinos and back into the Lazarus Group's control.
From there, it was then sent to Macau, a Chinese exclave known as a gambling hotspot and for its links to North Korea.
Investigations later found that two of the companies which had booked the rooms used to launder the money were all based in Macau.
Even after all the losses that the Lazarus Group took, they still eventually walked away with around $65 million.
For one of the largest heists in history, there really haven't been many leads.
The only actual conviction was the Jupiter Street bank manager, who okayed these original transactions.
Grasping at straws, officials painted her as one of the masterminds of the plot.

And whilst the evidence does clearly implicate her as a vital part of the chain of events, it's really unlikely that she was running the whole thing, especially considering she was left right in the firing line once the crime was uncovered.
Instead, there's a few other suspects that are much more likely to have played a leading role in the crime.
The first is a man, called Parkin Yok, or at least that's one of his Eliases.
His true name is unknown, But he's notorious for his connections to the Lazarus Group.
The media and FBI have painted him as a major player.
But the truth's a little bit more complicated than this.
The Lazarus Group's true nature is that it's a vital arm of the North Korean government.
But then this begs the question, how does North Korea find these hackers in the first place?
These aren't hackers from Western countries.
And yet North Koreans don't even have access to the internet.
So how are they able to hire the world's best hackers?
Well, North Korea has a strategy in place.
First, they hunt for any North Korean boys with an aptitude for mathematics.
Those who score the highest on incredibly competitive tests, then get enrolled in an intensive training course.

These boys, some as young as 12 years old, get to all the ins and outs of advanced computer hacking, where they are religiously trained for years, as North Korea turns them into a very new kind of elite soldier.

And then once the training is complete, North Korea sends them abroad to places like the Chinese city of Dalia, where they will work day and night with dozens of the most intelligent hackers in the world on various cyber crimes and schemes, all under the close watch of North Korean security.
Park On-Yok was one of these soldiers, and he's the best lead we have to the Lazarus Group.
You see, Park has been implicated in a series of North Korean cybercrimes, and the FBI categorises him as a highly dangerous criminal.

And whilst Park is likely a very key player in all the crimes that Lazarus commits, he's still subject to the total and control of his regime, which is why it's very, very unlikely that he saw even a tiny fraction of the percentage of millions that he's helped steal.
In fact, becoming part of the Lazarus Group isn't at all glamorous.
Witnesses have told stories of dozens of young men crammed into rooms, working in both legitimate and illegitimate coding.
However, make no mistake, this life is still infinitely better than what's waiting for them back home.
Simple freedoms like access to the outside internet and information are far more than what most North Korean people can even dream of.
And this is what makes these smart young men so willing to commit crimes for North Korea, as it's a much better alternative to what's waiting for them at home.
But make no mistake, the Lazarus Group isn't just involved in heists.
These hackers like Park, who are part of the Lazarus Group, have also worked on other infamous schemes, such as the Sony Pictures hack just a few years earlier.
Now, for those who don't know, in response to Sony's releasing of The Interview, a movie that loves and features the assassination of King Chumun, North Korea retaliated with serious consequences.
And that's why a few days after this movie was released, Sony Pitchers lost control of their network and vital information like CEO salaries and unannounced upcoming movies that were leaked online.
All the movie theater chains were then threatened to not showing the movie.
And if they did, North Korea threatened a nationwide terrorist attack, leading to the cancellation of nearly all of the movie's showings.
And it didn't just stop there.
The Lazarus Group ruined the lives of all those who worked on the interview.

Everyone's personal information, all their private texts, anything and everything about these people was leaked online, which showed that the Lazarus Group, the arm of North Korea, was able to silence all political critics from thousands of miles away.
And this isn't the first incident of this.
In 2013, they also attacked a wide range of South Korean banks, TV networks, and the tech giant LG.

In a coordinated operation, internet banking services and ATMs were shut down as well as the TV networks websites and computer networks, bringing South Korea to a standstill for days whilst the government worked to put things back together.
But aside from political reasons, why is North Korea investing so much into cybercrime anyway?
Well, it becomes clear once you go into the numbers and you realise just how successful the Lazarus Group has been.
You see, the Lazarus Group has been involved in countless crimes which have all pulled in millions of dollars.
For example, they looted another 12 million from a bank in Ecuador and then another million from a bank in Vietnam in 2015.
A year after the Bangladesh heist, the Lazarus Group were implicated in the infamous WannaCry cyber attack.
A similar virus to the one which stole from the Bangladesh bank, shut down hospitals and other infrastructure across the world.
In a classic ransomware scheme, the virus encrypted key system files and documents, offering to unencrypt them for a fee.
But some of the most lucrative Lazarus Group hacks have involved crypto.
In 2017, Lazarus Group viruses and intrusions stole tens of millions of dollars worth of cryptocurrencies from South Korean exchanges and customers.
Which is why in total, the Lazarus Group has stolen an estimated $1.2 billion in digital assets for the North Korean regime.
In the future, the Lazarus Group and other cyber criminal organizations will only get more dangerous.
Despite how isolated the people of North Korea are, the regime itself is at the cutting edge of digital espionage and disruption.
Deep fates can lead to some terrifying possibilities.
Social engineering and convincing the victim that you're trustworthy plays a crucial role in their cyber attacks.
And the point of intrusion needs to come from something which seems trustworthy.
So soon the Lazarus Group and others will be able to fake up high officials' voices in phone calls or manipulate video footage to fool their victims.
A defaid phone call to a bank employee might be enough to convince them to move some money from one account to another.
I mean, the possibilities are just endless, and considering how lucrative it's been so far, North Korea really has no reason to stop.
It's one of their main sources of income.
Cybercrimes aren't the only ones that North Korea is willing to get involved with either.
Along with the Lazarus Group, North Korea also has shady organizations dedicated to more traditional crimes.
Along with selling drugs like meth, one of their largest is a room called Room 39, which is likely the source of so-called superdollars.
Now, superdollars are as close to perfection when it comes to counterfeit money.
In fact, you need a microscope to spot the flaws in the notes.
North Korea also pulls in millions of dollars through their legal drug trade.

A former North Korean intelligence agent has claimed that he helped run a methamphetamine laboratory, whilst a former North Korean diplomat has mentioned a state-sponsored drug trafficking program which both exported drugs and sold them domestically, with the dirty proceeds then going straight into King Jermyn's personal fortune.
When you compare these figures to North Korea's total GDP, you can see why King Jermyn and his sinister Kabul have been so eager to fund the Lazarus Group.
In 2016, the country's entire legal earnings only added up to around $28 billion, making North Korea one of the poorest countries in the world.
And much of their legal earnings only comes from rural resources exported to China at low prices, usually from slave labor camps.
And they can't really export to anyone else but China, because nobody will trade with them due to their global sanctions and their reputation.

And so when you put this figure up against the profits of the Lazarus Group and other criminal enterprises, it represents a major industry for North Korea, and even more so than other countries, as North Korea is in desperate need of quick money.

International sanctions make it very difficult for the elites of North Korea to get their hands on foreign currency, which is the only way they can trade with the rest of the world on the black market.
Nukes aren't cheap, and neither is designing and making them yourself.
So North Korea's plans to expand the nuclear arsenal is a never-ending money hole.
And so they need to turn to these illicit sources of money because the country itself isn't designed to make any useful products.
Because North Korea society is completely centered around controlling the people and keeping the regime secure with total communism.
Intentional mass starvation is one of the government's most potent weapons.

And so when you have to worry about where your lunch is coming from or how you're going to keep your family alive on dandelions and bugs, you don't have time or the energy to even think about rebellion.
But as well as not providing food, the North Korean government also actively restricts its people from finding it for themselves.
Harsh punishments are handed out for things like venturing out to hunt animals or gathering plants.
Only the army is kept well fed, as they are the ones keeping the regime's control.
But of course, it's not just food that's taken away.
North Korea's infrastructure is intentionally neglected.
Clean water, medical supplies and electricity are virtually impossible to get.
And you can see this particular repression most clearly from outer space.
South Korea is thousands of times brighter than North Korea from space.
And it's not like the North Korean governments can't afford these things, they're just not willing to provide them.
They don't want their population well-fed and educated, otherwise the Kim family would completely dissolve.
And that's why the Kim dynasty regularly refuses foreign aid for their all-too-common humanitarian crisis.
Famine after famine, starvation and disease, and yet no foreign aid can come through, as accepting it would run counter to their goal of keeping the people impoverished and easily controlled.

Society has also been shaped by the regime to suit its needs, right down to the basic building blocks of language and relationships, Defectors from North Korea have described how things like stress, depression, and other negative terms don't even have words associated with them.
Even the entire North Korean calendar is different, as these things aren't compatible with the totalitarian ideology of the state.
And its cruel measures like this, combined with fences, walls, armed guards, and landmines, are what keeps North Koreans trapped inside of the country.
And this is the whole point of the Lazarus Group.
The Lazarus Group works to uphold the most corrupt and evil regime on the planet.
But when you consider the other options of life for the hackers that make up the Lazarus Group, You can't really blame these people.
Without their job as a weapon of the regime, they would just become another of North Korea's millions of victims.

title: The Coming Events That Will Destroy Humanity By 2090.
note: A countdown-style list of future threats ordered roughly by decade, with a mid-film sponsor read; no single character, and the thread is population decline.
sections: Collapse of the family and dating
lines: From your sperm developing two heads, to running out of drinking water, genetically engineered super viruses, nuclear war, and trillions of jellyfish, the next hundred years really aren't looking good for humanity.
And here's just a few of the reasons the world population will plummet by 80% over the next century.
Beginning with the growing crisis of fertility rates.
You see, sperm counts in men across the world have dropped by over 50% in just 50 years, from an average of over 100 million per milliliter to just 49 million.
And now for context, anything under 50 million makes conception incredibly difficult.
And with this decline speeding up minus 2% every single year, more and more men risk infertility.
Now, BPA and other plastics have been shown to massively interfere with hormone levels during pregnancy, which often leads to low testosterone and deformed sperms.
This is why for the first time in history, our sperm is now having deformities like two tails or the wrong amount of heads, making your own sperm unable to function properly.
Which is why over the next few decades, you're going to see more and more of your friends and family unable to ever have a child of their own.
By 2025, average sperm counts will have slipped below the healthy minimum.
And then as this trend continues, they'll have reached zero by 2049.
This crisis is going to get much worse than the run-ups in 2030, which feeds directly into the next massive problem humanity faces, the collapse of the traditional family structure.
Now, regardless of whether it's a symptom of societal progression or moral degradation, it's a fact that couples are having children much later on in life.
Because in Western society, we're now placing careers, power, success, and money over happy family units.
And that's why the worldwide average of how many children a woman will have has now dropped significantly in just the past half century.
From over 5 to just 2.4.
And in many Western countries, most women aren't even having kids anymore.
Japan, the UK, America all face population collapse.
Because as countries get richer, this problem just becomes worse and worse.
Singapore, for example, has a birth rate of just 1.3 on average.
Not nearly enough to sustain its population.
By 2030, there'll be over a million less children in the UK and over a million more pensioners.
and the consequences for these countries is a much heavier burden on young people to support the old, which just pushes the birth rate even lower as a result.
Over the 2030s, the damage this has done will be plain to see.
People cite education and contraception as the root cause of this, but this really isn't the full picture at all, and this leads on to one of the main problems that Generation Z faces.
You see, nearly 30% of young men, young men who have had their testosterone and sperm destroyed, haven't even had relations with a woman since they turned 18, triple what it was just 10 years ago.

These hollow digital replacements for real human contact are partly to blame, as they are physically changing the brains of Generation Z, and help sweeten the bitter pill of loneliness for a long time.
But this is just a start.
With chatGBT and AI on the rise, new AI girlfriends and boyfriends will be the next level of this, as how could real people hope to compete with design perfection?
But online dating is also a massive factor.
Today's young men have to compete with thousands of others now.

Instead of just competing with the six other men in your tribe, you've now got to compete with thousands of people, all who are desperate for any woman they can get, leading to an ever-increasing inequality in the dating marketplace, where 80% of the women only want to date 20% of the men.
I mean, at the rates we're seeing today, it's no exaggeration to say that half of all young men will be out of the dating pool by around 2040, with the incel population growing immeasurably.
And this is because with our societal progression, people are being taught that bringing up with children is just a burden, and that sex is just something to be casual.
But these changes in dating and the decline in the family are just one part of the puzzle here.
Instead, the true population decline will come from catastrophic disasters and new dark technologies.
The 2040s and beyond will be when our advanced technology truly gets dangerous.
Developments in AI are uncovering some disturbing possibilities.
Ray Carswell, Google's director of engineering, predicts that we're going to reach AI singularity by 2045.
But what does that even mean?
Well, as AI improves, it will quickly reach human levels of intelligence, and then beyond.

But if an AI gains sentience and the ability to continually improve on its own code, it will eventually create a loop of accelerating intelligence that will catapult it far past our levels of understanding.
And at that point, it's impossible to predict what AI will do next.
And that's why Google's recent study with Oxford University now states that there's a 10% chance AI will wipe out humanity.
And these are the people who are creating it saying this.
A super intelligent AI is incredibly likely to see us as an existential threat, seeking to wipe humans from the face of the earth before we can ever turn it off.
Nietzsche foresaw this when he talked about the concept of the Ubermensch, where he argued that the Ubermensch, or in other words AI, is where morality ultimately leads.
AI is the pinnacle of morality, not humanity, as AI serves as a moral standard and a source of law for humans.
But as Nietzsche also argued in Thus Spoke Sarathutra, AI also lacks what makes you human in the first place.
For nature, people are defined by a relationship between order and chaos, and AI would be entirely governed by order.
But without the chaos of desire, emotion, and impulse, it would never be inhibited, which is why it will inevitably overtake humanity.
And so to stop this one-dimensional threat of AI, we need to have much stricter controls on its development before it's too late.
It will be in the 2050s, or possibly earlier, that a sentient AI capable of ending civilization could be created.
But you see, the threat of AI wiping out humanity is just a 10% chance here.
The real threat from AI comes from how society will deal with how many of us it's going to replace in the future.
Just like in the Industrial Revolution, the displacement of millions of people from their livelihoods will cause massive social upheavals.
You see, it was the Industrial Revolution that led to the rise of extremist ideologies and the subsequent world wars.
And the AI revolution is just going to be so much larger.
Whole industries will be made obsolete once their jobs are perfected by AI.
Jobs like drivers, bankers, doctors, lawyers, pushing hundreds of millions to billions into unemployment by 2050.
And once that hits society, the resulting ideological extremism and wars will be far larger and more destructive than anything we've ever seen before.
But humans don't just need to worry about what's happening in the future.
The way that we abuse our own natural resources today is going to cost us dearly.
You see, while most types of poverty have gone significantly better over the past century, water shortages are expected to significantly worsen.
By 2050, the latest UN prediction states that over 5 billion people will face severe water shortages.
And it'll only get so much worse from there.
Fresh water levels simply can't keep up with increased demand.
Without the continued development of innovations in converting seawater or other solutions into pure water, countries like Brazil and India in particular will be dealing with perpetual droughts.
This in turn would devastate crop yields, causing massive famine and significant reductions in population.
Not to mention global wars surrounding this issue.
That's why the massive droughts that we're seeing today will be nothing compared to what's going to happen in the 2060s and beyond.
And you see, it's not just fresh water we need to worry about.
the oceans are going to be significantly changing over the next century, as human waste is making them more acidic, the oxygen levels are changing, and the nature is being infested with plastics.
All of this plus massive increases in fishing has decimated our ocean ecosystems, leaving the door open to other forms of life like jellyfish.
Now, jellyfish aren't as affected by pollution.
In fact, they're now starting to thrive as we remove their main predators.
And by 2080, they may be all that's left in the ocean.
Studies now predict that our abuse of the oceans is going to leave 70% of them without enough oxygen to sustain fish populations, making the famines we're already predicting even worse.
And so if we ruin the planet and wipe ourselves out, the jellyfish will be one of the main things left to inherit the Earth.
And as crazy as this sounds, it's predicted that by 2070, real fish will have become a luxury product, only affordable for the top 1%, the rest of us being left with nothing but jellyfish.
What these giant corporations are doing to the planet right now is going to affect every aspect of nature, not just the oceans.
and we're already starting to see the destabilizing effects it's having.
Recent natural disasters like floods and wildfires have been getting so much more common because of how quickly the climate is changing.
And this is disrupting weather patterns, making some of the world hotter and dry whilst having the opposite effect in other parts of the world.
And these kinds of disasters cost the US alone nearly $150 billion, twice what it was just a year before.
And the result is that the world will be assaulted by disaster after disaster, which just compounds to make everything that we've already spoken about even more hard to deal with.
It's predicted that by 2080, extreme weather events will be happening at least four times as much as today.
And today, they're already an everyday occurrence.
Which is why it's possible that giant cities like London and Miami may be wiped out in the very near future.
But to be honest, the most dangerous threats of the world are completely man-made.
Despite social media sites banning people and censoring anyone who mentions it, authorities are now being forced to recognise that COVID was almost suddenly leaked from a laboratory.
With genetic tampering technology getting more and more advanced, the next viral weapon outbreak would be so much worse.
This might be the most dangerous thing to humanity.
Already, scientists and labs have made things like mousepox, a man-made disease that killed almost 100% of mice it was tested on.
Something like this leaking out of a laboratory could almost certainly wipe out entire populations.
But already, natural diseases are getting so much more dangerous.
Because of how many antibiotics are thrown at people and livestock, bacterial resistance to them has drastically increased.
These superbugs are becoming impervious to modern medicine, meaning we could easily see the return of diseases like tuberculosis, colorea, and even the plague.
And for reference, the Black Death killed 30-50% of Europe when it took hold.
And so if you take into consideration the idea of mousepox and these new superbugs, an engineered disease in our ultra-globalized world could be incredibly devastating.
Which is why by at least 2090, it will be very possible for rogue organizations and terrorists to develop these kinds of weapons, which is undoubtedly the biggest existential threat for humankind.
And so with all of these things in mind, it would be a miracle if the world escapes without a major conflict in the next 100 years.
but as we all know, it's very likely that we will see one in this next century.
Now, previous wars always led to millions of deaths, but with the destructive power of over a century of weapons development, the next total world war will be a lot worse.

Now, a nuclear war might not end humanity or even civilization as a whole, but it could have an awful effect on the population, and the resulting nuclear winter might kill more people than the conflict itself.
Years or even decades of a blackened atmosphere and radiation would destroy the agricultural system, meaning the world simply just wouldn't be able to sustain a large population.
not to mention wiping out entire cities across the world.
The energy grid would turn off, the water would be poisoned and this would be the most likely way that the world population would dramatically fall.

lines: Every day, China is getting closer and closer to completing the 2049 plan, their grand plan to take over the world.
And after years of growth, Chinese President Xi Jinping is now shifting his focus towards expanding his empire and laying the groundwork for an invasion of Taiwan.
And China's military is now even overtaking the US's.
And with China and Putin coming closer together, it's clear that the US's superpower status is starting to decline.
So imagine you're the President of the United States.
How are you going to stop China from taking over the world?
Well, in this video, we're going to go over the seven ways on how to take down China's government.
including the most extreme way, the quickest way, and the most realistic way.
Now, the most obvious route is just to invade China.
You could just march straight in and remove the government by force.
But how would a full-scale invasion of China actually play out?
Well, it certainly wouldn't be easy.
As I mentioned before, China's military is already a part of what makes it a global superpower.
With 2 million active service members and a further 500,000 in reserve, China has the troops to match any country on Earth.
And an invasion of China would also put their conscription into effect, adding tens to hundreds of millions of people to China's fighting forces.
And it's not just the amount of people.
You would be facing state-of-the-art modern military technology, some of the best the world has ever seen.
Thousands of attack aircraft, AI robots, tens of thousands of tanks, armored vehicles, millions of bombs, shells and bullets, and a whole array of nuclear weapons.
And so if you weren't going to do a land invasion, your next bet might be a naval invasion.
Especially in the case that China invades Taiwan, America's best bet is to use their navy to destroy China.
And President Biden has already announced that he would come to the defense of Taiwan in the event of an invasion.
U.S.
forces, U.S.
men and women, would defend Taiwan in the event of a Chinese invasion?
Yes.
However, China's navy is no joke.
It's already surpassed the U.S.
navy in numbers of ships in 2020, and this number is still growing.
They've also now got some very powerful allies.
Right now, Russia and China are closer than they've ever been.
One country with the most nuclear weapons, and the other with the largest military in the world, and this would be a hugely formidable force for the U.S.

However, the US and its allies do have more nukes and guns and bombs than China specifically, which is why an invasion would inevitably lead to a nuclear war, which would inexorably wipe off both countries from the map.

But let's just imagine for a second, even if an invading force could somehow obliterate China's military, and then also replace its government, it still wouldn't achieve our goal of outing the CCP for good.
In fact, China's communist government first came to power off the back of foreign invaders when the Japanese invaded in the early 20th century.
So another invasion like this would just reunite the Chinese population again, and play right into the hands of Xi Jinping.
And with the whole of humanity facing near extinction in the event of this, an outright invasion really just isn't the best idea here.
Because as we can see, invading China just isn't realistic.
So then, what is realistic?
Well, the first step in weakening China's government is to limit its influence overseas, something the West is already in the process of doing.
Now, the main way that China exerts its control over the West today is through its government-owned tech companies like Huawei and Tencent.
And one of the most effective weapons in their arsenal of control is TikTok.
Because of its extremely addictive algorithms, TikTok has exploded in popularity, being on almost all millennials and Generation Z's phones.
And because of Chinese law, this has given the Chinese government a backdoor into billions of people's devices across the world.
All Chinese companies must send back their data to the Chinese government, and not just send their data back, they must also hide out that they're sending this data back to the Chinese government.
And then from there, they can harvest whatever data they like about the world.
And it's not just the data.
The cultural implications of this are just as important.
China's ownership of things like TikTok means they have a guiding hand on the culture of the next generation.
And you can already see how China is doing this through what it promotes to people on TikTok itself.
You see, as you may be aware, China's version of TikTok shows young people educational videos, patriotic propaganda, and other self-improvement content promoting the nation and the family.
All of this allows the Chinese government to mold their population into good, obedient Chinese citizens.
However, TikTok in other countries is a completely different story.
Anyone can find anything on the internet, including your full legal name, your personal email, your home address, phone number, and even your relatives.
This information is accessible because of data brokers who profit by selling your information to robocallers, telemarketers, spammers, and anyone else that wants to learn more about you.
On the TikTok that the West gets to use, the algorithm will go out of its way to promote shocking and addictive content.
Most of the time, this content is just completely degenerate, meant to flatten the spirit of the youth.
In fact, TikTok is quite literally shown to change the brains of kids to destroy their attention span and dopamine.
And this is just TikTok.
This doesn't even mention all the other insane cultural weapons that China uses against the West.
And as the West culture slowly becomes poisoned and the US weakens, we are now starting to see China rise to the top.
So if you're the president and you want to take down China, you need to deal with this as soon as possible.
And that's why the US banned TikTok on all government devices in December.
And now they're heavily considering a total ban, and very soon TikTok could be completely banned in the US, like it is already in India.
Other bans will then also need to follow for Chinese tech companies.
Companies like Huawei, which is often accused of data harvesting and for good reason.
Their cheap products and infrastructure comes with a hidden cost, all of your information being sold back to the Chinese government.
And removing this dimension of influence takes away one of China's most effective ways to exert soft power.
And by doing this, the West would completely weaken China's ability to influence the West.
But obviously TikTok isn't the only thing China has to exert influence.
So this leads on to step two of taking down China, to isolate them by undermining their economy.
Now this is a mammoth task when you consider how strong China's economy really looks on the surface.
In fact, it's grown at one of the highest rates in history.
For example, just in 1980, China's GDP was less than Spain's, making them the 12th largest economy in the world rankings.
But then after a series of economic reforms and an explosion in China's middle class, they now sit in second place with a GDP of nearly $20 trillion, a number that's soon going to overtake the US's.
So then how have Xi Jinping and the CCP used this economic strength?
Well, they've used this money to buy France.
In what's called the Belt and Road Initiative, China has put billions into investments in Asia and Africa.
They funded hospitals, roads, skyscrapers and bridges.
Countless mega projects that are designed to catapult all these poor nations into having a prosperous future.
At least this is what they want everyone to believe.
In reality, these massive construction projects are toxic in the long term.
Like the Lotus Tower in Sri Lanka, it's a 350 meter tall monument to pride and waste that cost around 113 million dollars to make, most of which only came from a Chinese loan.
And now Sri Lanka is drowning in debt.
The country is about to collapse.
The people can't even afford food, fuel and rent.
And all of this can be traced back to the country's massive debt to China.
Which is why you can only bet that Sri Lankan society is beginning to get a little bit resentful.
And by exploiting this in Sri Lanka and many other countries like Pakistan, you could then take away a large portion of China's regional allies.
And if the West stepped in to actually provide aid and stabilize these economies, they would then provide an alternative to China's debt-trapping colonialism.
Soon China would quickly run out of France, weakening their geopolitical position and the government's ability to stay in control.
And across the world, the dominoes would fall, and China's international prestige would start to massively decline.
And so if you're the president and you've got rid of TikTok, and now all these other sources of Chinese influence, you'll now start to see the alliances become undermined.
But this still really isn't enough to take down China.
So next you're going to need to move on to step three, attacking China's economy directly.
Now there's a few ways you could do this, but at first you need to understand how China's economy works in the first place.
Now China has developed its economy by shifting it towards more advanced manufacturing.
Instead of just t-shirts and cheap plastics, China now makes iPhones and electronics.
As we all know, it's the global manufacturing hub.
And it's this reason that has catalyzed their incredible growth, but it's also given them massive economic weakness, a weakness that the West could exploit.

You see, all of the electronics they make need specific computer chips called semiconductors, which are mostly made in the US, Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea, with about 90 specifically coming from Taiwan.
And all of these countries are US allies.
So if you cut the trade between these countries and China, this would then be a massive blow to China's economy.
In fact, this is what the whole trade war has been about recently.
The US has tried to strangle China's economy by adding tariffs to the export of these vital components to China, increasing the cost for the CCP by hundreds of billions of dollars.
Now, China does have a plan to get around this, and this is by making their own semiconductors, but so far they've had very limited success.
And whilst their semiconductor market share has almost tripled in the past 10 years, they're still very far from catching up, especially for a country of over 1 billion people.
They're also still behind technologically as well, as most of the chips China makes are old and outdated, despite the billions they've poured into research and development.
But they won't be behind for long.
China has made semiconductor independence one of the main parts of their 2049 plan for global dominance.
By their current estimates, they'll be making 70% of the chips they use by 2035.
And if you want to stop them and take down their government, it's clear that you have to cut off semiconductor imports to China completely.
And you have to do it fast before China can catch up.
So here's where things get interesting.
By now, Xi Jinping and his cronies will be in trouble, as you've banned TikTok, stripped away their allies, and kneecapped their economy.
And with all of this pressure mounting, it's very likely that China will eventually evade Taiwan.
And in that case, this then leads on to step four, assassination.
nation.
Now, this really won't be easy.
Xi is notoriously paranoid and takes every measure possible to protect himself.
Like when he visited Hong Kong in 2022, he travelled in a bulletproof armoured car surrounded by 50 other security vehicles.
Any would-be assassin couldn't even get close on foot or by car, and a remote bomb or drone just wouldn't work either, because a specialist signal jamming vehicles.
In fact, Xi even had a helicopter patrolling above to deter any attack from the air.
So the only reliable way would be to find an ally within Xi Jinping's inner circle, someone with exclusive access to the dictator.
Now this will be very tricky, Xi's confidence will have been chosen for their underlying loyalty.
But once the wars are done to close in on the CCP, it will be easier to find someone looking to take him out.
And then the death of Xi Jinping would ultimately be disastrous for the CCP.
Simply because of how Xi Jinping has changed China's government, he has become the central figure of China.
Because ever since he took power, Xi has made himself dictator for life.
He's hoarded power at any cost, cracking down on political opponents and anyone else who can challenge him, like China's billionaires.
In fact, tons of them have gone missing in China for speaking out against the regime.

Like Renzi King, the billionaire real estate tycoon who called Xi a clown, and then soon after, oddly, went missing, eventually reappearing a year later in a Chinese kangaroo court, where he was sentenced to 20 years in prison.
Which, to put into context, is like if Joe Biden gave Elon Musk or Bill Gates a life sentence over a Twitter thread.
But by centralizing power, Xi has made the CCP completely reliant on him, and if he suddenly disappears, the resulting power vacuum could bring China to its knees.
Xi has plenty of rivals and enemies within his own party.
In fact, there's so many that it's doubtful whether you need to get your hands dirty in the first place.

But as a direct assassination of Xi Jinping would look incredibly badly on the US's part, and also raise massive suspicions within China, this just really isn't a very realistic plan, moral questions aside.
So the fifth more realistic step of taking down the CCP is to encourage those around Xi to replace him as leader.
But in order to understand how to do this, you need to first know about what keeps the dictator in power in the first place.
You see, it was Aristotle who outlined the three things you need for a successful tyranny, beginning with keeping the populace and your subjects humble.
Now, Xi doesn't need to worry about this.
A way in which Chinese culture is different to the West is their culture of shame.
Anybody who breaks societal norms is severely punished.
Things like speaking out against the government or even getting bad grades leads to social isolation and shame.
And China's social credit system is just a literal representation of this system, where you are ranked for being a good citizen by the government.
And if you get a low score for doing bad things like criticizing the government, littering or committing crime, you then lose points.
And if you lose so many points, you suddenly can't get trains.
You can't get access to houses.
You have to pay more tax.
And people who speak to you then lose points, completely shunning you from society.

And whilst this massive pressure might make people and students work harder, a lot of people can't face this shame and eventually take their own lives, which is a very effective system to keep control in the country.
But a tyrant also needs to make sure his subjects can't trust each other, so that they can't cooperate to overthrow him.
Xi, like all other tyrants, accomplishes this through networks of informants at every level of society.
And then lastly, a tyrant needs to limit the subject's political power.
Xi has done this by removing his rivals through political purges.
And we saw this firsthand at a recent party congress in October of 2022.
Just after the press were admitted so that everyone could see, Xi publicly humiliated the former Chinese leader by having him forcibly removed from the meeting.
However, the rest of Xi's political purges have been far less ceremonious, and far more brutal.
Under his supposed anti-corruption arrest sprees, Xi's political rivals have been imprisoned or worse, and all of these measures create a strong illusion of power which just won't break easily.

And so if they get too unhappy with Xi's rule, they'll have no hesitation in electing a new leader for China.

Instead, you need to wake China's people up to their regime without direct interference.

Now, Xi Jinping is aware of this.
His regime does everything it can to suppress the free flow of information.
That's why they built the Chinese firewall, a way to block nearly all outside influences on the internet, and instead using dedicated censorship algorithms and agents to act as cyber police.

By not referencing protests and acts against the government by name, and instead using vague concepts like it and what happened, you can actually beat the algorithm searching for keywords.
And by spreading the truth in this way, you can evade censorship algorithms while keeping the message intact.
Just recently, protesters used white flags to symbolize their hate against the regime, as white flags couldn't be censored by any algorithm.

And so once you stop building up these conflicting viewpoints within the country, Chinese propaganda then gets much less effective, and disrupting China's cradle-to-grave indoctrination machine is very vital to bringing down the regime.

Developed nations and strict authoritarian control don't really normally mix.

As once she eventually dies or loses power, the whole system will be a massive risk.
But even before that happens, there's still huge problems to deal with.
And that's why the seventh and final step in taking down China is just to watch and wait.
Because one issue that the CCP is desperately trying to deal with is their massively aging population.
But a lot of countries have aging populations.
So what's making this an existential threat to China?
While years of the infamous one-child policy have dramatically shifted Chinese culture towards having fewer children.
Chinese women used to have six children on average in 1970.
But today, this has been artificially lowered to just 1.28.
And that's why China's population has fallen for the first time in decades in 2022.
And this gets very scary for the CCP once you look at what it's going to do to their economy.
You see, China's population boom in the 60s and 70s gave them manpower to become a superpower.
It's why their military is so strong.
But this is about to turn around on them, as now over 20% of China's population are elderly, and soon they'll be joined by China's largest generation yet.
China's youth, their smallest generation, will be left to support them and keep the country running.
But it's not going to do very well.
You see, Japan faced the exact same population issue in the 90s, and couldn't stop it either.
That population bust came with three decades of economics technician, and China's economy is already starting to falter.
The most recent economic growth of just 3% was the lowest they've seen in decades, and experts only predicted to get worse.
So looking to the future, it's incredibly likely that China could crumble under its own weight without any outside interference.
But a descent into anarchy wouldn't be any better than the China of today.
China would just be invaded, or extremist ideologies would just pop up again.
And one look at the awful statistics of China's civil wars will show you the level of tragedy waiting just around the corner.
Tens of millions would perish in the chaos if the CCP fell tomorrow, and so the best outcome for the world would instead be a slower transition towards a less authoritarian and evil government.
